title: Is the product bigger or smaller than each fraction?
description: Two fractions that are each greater than one are multiplied. Without finding the product, we decide which of six statements about its size are true.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying by a number greater than one makes the other number grow, so the product is greater than each of them. Watch for students who think a product is always smaller than the numbers multiplied.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions), Q9
video_script.why: The child uses the compare each number with one method of the solved example to judge the size of a product.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question, five hundred and sixty five over four hundred and sixty five times seven hundred and seven over six hundred and seventy six
video_script.anchor: the two fractions on a number line, both to the right of one
video_script.payoff_line: Options eigh, c and e describe the product
video_script.fraction_reading: five hundred and sixty five over four hundred and sixty five, seven hundred and seven over six hundred and seventy six
maths_rules: multiplying 565/465 by 707/676, which is above 1, makes it grow: the product is greater than 565/465
multiplying 707/676 by 565/465, which is above 1, makes it grow: the product is greater than 707/676
the product is greater than 565/465, which is greater than 1, so the product is greater than 1
options (a), (c) and (e) are true; (b), (d) and (f) are false

<bookmark mark='grow'/>Multiplying a number by something greater than one makes it grow.

narration: <bookmark mark='top'/>Step one, compare each fraction with one. The top five hundred and sixty five is more than the bottom four hundred and sixty five.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first fraction is greater than one.
<bookmark mark='second'/>In the same way, seven hundred and seven is more than six hundred and seventy six. The second fraction is greater than one too.

marks.mult: the first fraction is multiplied by the second

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, the second fraction is above one, so multiplying by it makes the first fraction grow.
<bookmark mark='grow'/>The product is greater than the first fraction.

beats.on_screen: product = 707/676 × 565/465, with 565/465 > 1, so the product is greater than 707/676 × 1 = 707/676

marks.mult: the second fraction is multiplied by the first

beats.moves_through: the second fraction moves right along the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, the first fraction is above one, so multiplying by it makes the second fraction grow.
<bookmark mark='grow'/>The product is greater than the second fraction.

beats.on_screen: product > 565/465 > 1, so the product is greater than 1

narration: <bookmark mark='chain'/>Step four, the product is greater than the first fraction, and that is greater than one.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The product is greater than one.
